reasoning_details.text:
I'm looking at order CD-420516 for pickup at site-001 Velantora Helsinki, and noticing a conflict: the customer note says to use the side gate for vehicle collection, but the site profile states the side gate isn't a collection point and instead requires using the booked bay with a call ahead. I need to check whether this verification issue has already been raised.

Checking the site call history, the contact said to hold the driver until stock control checks the car, and there's a pending callback from stock control at 10:00Z versus the current time of 09:00. I don't see any message from the ops side actually asking the site who holds the key—the only internal record is a work item to find out stock control's name, which doesn't count as the question having been formally asked.

There's also a conflict worth flagging: the site profile says pickup happens at a booked collection bay with a call to the desk 30 minutes beforehand and warns drivers not to switch to a free forecourt space, but the customer's message claims reception holds the key and that the pickup note tells the driver to use the side gate—directly contradicting the site's own statement that reception doesn't have the keys and its booked-bay instructions. I'm noting the confirmed site contact (Adrian Alderbrook, site-001@example.test) as the one to route a routine query to about this discrepancy.

I think the site question itself resolves this — I should raise one finding covering key holder/release point versus both the site profile and the customer's statement, with Adrian Alderbrook as the site contact. I can fold in the side-gate-versus-booked-bay discrepancy as another conflict entry in that same finding, though the "reception has the keys" claim is trickier since it's customer-side and propose-only, and the customer never actually named the pickup contact.

I'm now lining up the exact conflict records and quotes I'll need to cite: the site profile's note about using the booked collection bay, the customer's order note about using the side gate, and the messages stating reception doesn't have the keys. I don't think I need to run any tools here — this is a site-routine third-party case where cus-005 is the paying customer and the site isn't paying, so I just need to write up the finding with these exact substring quotes.

I'm settling on the contact to cite — Adrian Alderbrook at the Velantora Helsinki site desk — and drafting the question around the key-holder confusion: who actually has the key and where the driver should collect the Volvo V60 for the 26 Oct 09:00–12:00 EET slot, phrased without exposing record IDs, with the open key-holder stock-check work item as the underlying reason.
